claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 18 and doesn't live with me at the moment, but I do help support him financially.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand his situation better.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he attending college, sixth form, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's doing his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in approved education (A-levels), that's a good sign for eligibility.

You mentioned Alex doesn't live with you at the moment. **Can you tell me where Alex is currently living?** (For example, is he living with another parent, a relative, in student accommodation, or somewhere else?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living with his dad, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is living with his dad, I need to understand the current Child Benefit arrangement.

**Is anyone currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, is his dad claiming it, or is no one claiming it at the moment?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his dad isn't claiming it. No one is claiming Child Benefit for Alex at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You mentioned you help support Alex financially. This is important for eligibility when a child lives with someone else.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions?** (For example, do you pay for things like clothes, pocket money, food, or contribute towards his accommodation? And is this weekly, monthly, or in another arrangement?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute towards his upkeep every week - I help with things like his clothes, travel costs, and give him some money for lunch and things he needs. It works out to about £26 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail. That's very helpful.

Just to confirm a couple more things:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex working at all, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working. He's just focusing on his studies at the moment.

conversation.text:
## Good News!

**You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Alex qualifies** - Even though he's 18, he's still eligible because he's in approved education (A-levels) and is under 20 years old.

✓ **You're contributing enough** - Although Alex lives with his dad, you're contributing approximately £26 per week towards his upkeep (clothes, travel, lunch money, etc.). This meets the requirement that you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment.

✓ **No one else is claiming** - Since Alex's dad isn't claiming Child Benefit and no one else is, you're able to make a claim.

✓ **Alex isn't working** - He's focusing on his studies and isn't working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in his own right.

✓ **You live in the UK** - You're resident in Manchester, which satisfies the residency requirement.

### What to do next:

You can make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. When you apply, you'll need to explain that Alex lives with his father but you're contributing to his upkeep.

**One important note:** If you or Alex's dad have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

Therefore, the mother is eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.
